heroSummary: The Bambu Lab P1S requires a hardened steel nozzle and hardened extruder gear upgrade before processing abrasive Polymaker Fiberon PA612-CF15. Once upgraded, it reliably achieves safe speeds up to 143 mm/s capped by a conservative 12 mm³/s volumetric flow limit.
bedSurfaceRecommendation: Bambu Textured PEI Plate with PVA glue stick or Magigoo PA release agent
slicerTweaks: Set the Maximum Volumetric Speed cap to 12 mm³/s to prevent severe underextrusion due to high carbon fiber melt viscosity.
Configure Nozzle Temperature to 285°C for all layers and Bed Temperature to 50°C to match Polymaker's low-warpage PA612 formulation.
Tune Pressure Advance to roughly 0.038 and set Retraction Distance to 0.8 mm at 30 mm/s to eliminate fiber oozing.
Enable 'Avoid Crossing Walls' and set Outer Wall Speed to 80 mm/s to ensure clean surface matte consistency and dimensionally accurate perimeters.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Rapid nozzle wear and inconsistent extrusion diameter
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Abrasive 15% carbon fiber reinforcement eroding the stock Bambu P1S stainless steel nozzle.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Install the official Bambu Lab 0.4mm Hardened Steel Hotend assembly and Hardened Steel Extruder Gears.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Brittle layer bonding and Z-axis splitting
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Excessive auxiliary/part cooling fan speed cooling the nylon extrudate below its fusion threshold.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Cap maximum part cooling fan to 25%, turn off the auxiliary chamber fan completely, and keep the P1S door closed.

troubleshootingMatrix.issue: Rough fuzzy texture, popping noises, and stringing
troubleshootingMatrix.rootCause: Hygroscopic PA612 polymer matrix saturated with atmospheric moisture.
troubleshootingMatrix.exactFix: Dehydrate the spool in a filament dryer at 80°C for 8 to 12 hours prior to printing, and print directly from a sealed dry container.

faq.question: Can I feed Polymaker Fiberon PA612-CF15 directly through the Bambu AMS?
faq.answer: Yes, but prolonged use will wear the standard plastic AMS funnel inlets; use wear-resistant ceramic/PTFE guides or feed from an external drybox.

faq.question: Why is the recommended bed temperature set to only 50°C for a nylon filament?
faq.answer: PA612 has significantly lower crystallization shrinkage than pure PA6, allowing it to adhere stably at 45-55°C without warping when using proper bed adhesives.

faq.question: What will happen if I attempt to print this on the stock P1S hotend?
faq.answer: The abrasive carbon fibers will erode the stock stainless steel nozzle within a few hundred grams, enlarging the orifice and ruining dimensional accuracy.

faq.question: Does the P1S need an actively heated chamber for this material?
faq.answer: No, the enclosed passive chamber of the P1S combined with bed radiation is sufficient due to the low-shrinkage chemical backbone of PA612.
